title: Prime Agents may run Allocation Instances with secret proprietary strategies, unlike every other Sky Primitive
content:
A.2.2.10.1.1.3.1 states that Prime Agent teams "may choose to directly operationalize their Allocation System Primitive Instances... using internal, proprietary strategies that are not defined in their Artifacts," and flags this as "an exception to the general rule that Operational Executor Agents operationalize all Sky Primitives on behalf of Prime Agents."

The exception exists because allocation is the one Primitive where the *strategy itself* is the value added. Publishing an edge in an Artifact destroys it — competitors and counterparties read the Atlas. Every other Primitive is process, where transparency costs nothing and buys accountability.

What replaces disclosure is outcome measurement plus a takeover trigger: self-operationalizing Primes "will be required to formulate KPIs for their proprietary strategies; should an Instance under-perform these KPIs, Operational GovOps is authorized to step in and operationalize the Instance(s) via a back-up strategy that is defined in the Agent Artifact."

That is the structural move worth generalising. Opacity is licensed only where a *substitute* is pre-positioned: the back-up strategy must be in the Artifact even though the live one is not, so the ecosystem always has a legible path to keep the Instance running without the Prime's cooperation. The concession is that the KPI threshold now carries all the weight a public strategy would have carried, and the Atlas admits the design is incomplete — "Additional logic on this point will be defined in a future iteration."
description: A named exception to Operational Executor Agent delegation: strategies need not appear in the Artifact, but the Prime must publish KPIs and a fallback strategy GovOps can activate on underperformance.
